title: 水调歌头
author: Su Shi

original: 明月几时有，把酒问青天
不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年
我欲乘风归去，又恐琼楼玉宇
高处不胜寒，起舞弄清影
不应有恨，何事长向别时圆
人有悲欢离合，月有阴晴圆缺
此事古难全，但愿人长久
translation: When did the bright moon first appear? I raise my wine to ask the blue sky
I wonder what year it is tonight in the palace halls of heaven
I wish to ride the wind and return there, but I fear those jade towers
So high up, I could not bear the cold — better to dance with my pure shadow
How much better to be in the mortal world
The moonlight passes through the red pavilion, slips by the ornate windows, shining on the sleepless
There should be no complaints — why then is the moon full when we are apart?
People have sorrow and joy, separation and reunion; the moon has dark and bright phases
This has never been perfect since ancient times — I only wish people stay well
Though a thousand miles apart, we share her beauty together

annotations.琼楼玉宇: jade towers — beautiful palaces in heaven
annotations.不胜寒: cannot bear the cold — loneliness in high places
annotations.婵娟: beauty, referring to the moon — the desire to be reunited with loved ones

appreciation: This is Su Shi's most famous poem, written on Mid-Autumn Festival when he was separated from his brother. The poem expresses longing for reunion while accepting the imperfection of life. The famous line 'May people live long, a thousand miles apart, sharing her beauty' has become a blessing for loved ones separated by distance.
